Supplementary files format and content: gene_counts.xlsx provides gene-level counts of reads unambiguously mapping to exons. There is one table for the reads assigned by Xenome to the Mus Musculus genome (originating from the mouse alveolar type 2 cells of the organoids in the well), and one table for the reads assigned to the Homo Sapiens genome (originating from the human fibroblasts of the organoids in the well).

Supplementary files format and content: imaging_outputs.csv contains the main outputs of the image analysis performed on each well at day 7 and day 14, in terms of number or organoids in the well, average area of the organoids in the well, and estimate of the percentage of the well covered by organoids.
Supplementary files format and content: plate_design.csv contains the sgRNA sequences used to target each gene and their location on the four plates.
Supplementary files format and content: xenome_stats.csv contains the summary of the sequencing read assignment made by Xenome (Conway et al., 2012).

The sequencing reads in each fastq file were first split between mouse and human using Xenome (Conway et al., 2012). Only reads unambiguously assigned to either mouse or human were kept and respectively aligned to their reference genome (mouse: GRCm38.p5, human: GRCh38.p10) through the HTSeqGenie v4.35 Bioconductor package (Pau and Reeder, 2012, https://doi.org/10.18129/B9.bioc.HTSeqGenie). First, reads with low nucleotide qualities (70% of bases with quality <23) or matches to rRNA and adapter sequences were removed. Then, reads were aligned using GSNAP (Wu et al., 2010; Wu et al., 2016) version ‘2013-10-10-v2’, allowing maximum of two mismatches per 75 base sequence (parameters: ‘-M 2 -n 10 -B 2 -i 1 -N 1 -w 200000 -E 1 --pairmax-rna=200000 --clip-overlap'). Transcript annotation was based on the Gencode genes database (human: GENCODE 27, mouse: GENCODE M15). Reads unambiguously mapping to exons were counted to get gene-level read counts.

Libraries were prepared from extracted RNA using a modified Smart-seq3 protocol ( Hagemann-Jensen, M., Ziegenhain, C., Chen, P. et al. Single-cell RNA counting at allele and isoform resolution using Smart-seq3. Nat Biotechnol 38, 708–714 (2020). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-020-0497-0) Annealing reaction was performed with 4ul purified RNA, 0.8 ul 40% PEG 8000, 0.08 ul RNAse Inhibitor, 0.04 ul Smart-seq3 oligo dT (100µM), 0.3 ul dNTP (25mM each) and 1 ul water per 384 well reaction. 10 ul mineral oil was added on top to prevent evaporation. Reaction was sealed, spun and incubated at 70˚C for 10 min. Reverse translation was performed by adding 2 ul of RT mix (0.2ul Tris HCl, pH8.0 (1M), 0.24 ul NaCl (1M), 0.2 ul MgCl2 (100mM), 0.08 ul GTP (10mM), 0.64 ul DTT (100mM), 0.16 ul TSO (100µM), 0.08 ul Maxima H Minus RTase and 0.4 ul water) to each 384 well reaction. The RT reaction was incubated at 42°C for 90 min and repeated the following steps for 10 cycles: 50˚C for 2 min and 42˚C for 2 min, and was terminated at 85°C for 5 min.

cDNA amplification was performed by adding 12ul of PCR mix (0.1 ul cDNA fwd (100µM), 0.02 ul cDNA rev (100µM), 0.1 ul MgCl2 (100mM), 10 ul 2X Kapa HiFi Hotstart Readymix  and 1.78 ul water) to the RT reaction for a total of 20 ul. Reaction was thermal cycled at 95°C for 3 min, [98°C for 20 sec, 65°C for 30 sec, 72°C for 4 min] x 14 cycles, 72 °C 4min. cDNA was diluted 1:10 in water. 1 ul of each sample was transferred to a new 384 well plate to perform tagmentation. 3 ul of tagmentation mix (0.8 ul 5X TAPS Mg buffer, 0.1 ul Tn5 enzyme, 2.1 ul water) was added to each sample on ice. Plate was sealed, vortexed for 15 seconds and spun. The reaction mixture was incubated at 55 °C for 10 min. Reaction was quenched by adding 0.5µl of 0.2% SDS to each well, sealing, vortexing for 15 seconds, and spinning the plate. The plate was  incubated at room temperature for 5 min. Libraries were indexed by added 3.5 ul of PCR mix and 2 ul indexing primers  to each sample.  Reaction was thermal cycled at 72°C for 5 min, 95°C for 3 min, [98°C for 20 sec, 65°C for 30 sec, 72°C for 30 sec] x 10 cycles, 72 °C 4min. Libraries were pooled and sequenced on an Illumina NovaSeq X Plus system, targeting 8M reads per library.
